title: Chung-Feller Theorem Overview
body: The Chung-Feller theorem (1949) states that among the C(2n,n) balanced lattice paths from (0,0) to (2n,0), exactly Cₙ have k upsteps above the x-axis, for each k ∈ {0,...,n}. The proof strategy uses the cycle lemma: prepending +1 converts a balanced path to a positive-sum sequence with exactly 1 good rotation.

title: Balanced Path Properties
body: IsBalancedPath l n requires: l has n copies of +1, n copies of -1, and all elements are ±1. This implies length 2n and sum 0, both proved using algebraic infrastructure from BallotProblemOQ01.

title: Prepend Connection to Cycle Lemma
body: The key bridge: prepending +1 to a balanced path gives a sequence with (n+1) ones and n negative-ones, which is an element of kCountedSequence 1 (n+1) n. The cycle lemma then applies directly, giving exactly 1 good rotation since (n+1) - 1·n = 1.

title: Counting Identity
body: The identity C(2n,n) = Cₙ × (n+1) follows directly from catalan_formula in BallotProblemOQ03.lean. Combined with the uniform distribution (axiom), this gives Cₙ paths per type.

title: Chung-Feller Uniform Distribution (Axiomatized)
body: The remaining axiom states that all n+1 path types have the same cardinality. The proof idea: each orbit of cyclic rotations visits exactly one path of each type, creating a uniform partition. Proving this requires explicitly tracking how cyclic shifts change the upstep-above-axis count.
